clue.text: Passed time, we hear, with eccentric, unexpected participant

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the first part is spelt differently from the way it sounds

parts.note: to while away time is to pass it idly
a card is a comical or eccentric person

explanation.surface: Someone idles about with an oddball who turned up out of nowhere at an event.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a wild card is an entrant admitted without qualifying, so an unforeseen competitor.

clue.text: You can't trust me about second love

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: the confession 'I do lie' is why you couldn't trust the speaker
S is the standard abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A self-confessed unreliable lover warns a partner about their latest affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'You can't trust me' stands for the spoken admission I DO LIE, which then goes round S.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to adore or worship them, a strong form of loving.

clue.text: Dishonest to free up openings for this year

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rid is to free, read upwards

indicators.note: openings are beginnings, so only the first letter of each word is wanted

parts.note: first letters of this and year

explanation.surface: Something underhand is needed to clear space in the calendar for this year.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty tricks or dirty money are dishonest, so the adjective is a common synonym.

clue.text: Duke to appear backing exciting political arrangement

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for appear is written in reverse

parts.note: to come is to appear, as in come into view
racy means lively or exciting

explanation.surface: A nobleman shows up in support of a thrilling new political settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Democracy is a system of government, an arrangement of political power held by the people.

clue.text: Feeble, uninteresting? i's pages cutting through that

indicators.note: cutting through tells us the letters for i and pages break into the word for uninteresting, the 'that' of the clue

parts.note: dry describes something dull and uninteresting
the letter i itself

explanation.surface: A reader complains that the pages of the i newspaper are feeble and dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British newspaper, but here it is just the letter I; I + PP goes 'cutting through' DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Drippy is informal for weak, sentimental and ineffectual, which matches feeble.

clue.text: 'Swiss city not vacantly blocking additional university' — Times

indicators.note: blocking tells us the emptied not sits in the middle of the word for additional

parts.note: more means additional or extra

indicators.note: vacantly tells us not is emptied of its middle, keeping only its ends

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a Swiss city and an extra university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacantly' empties not of its middle, and that pair is 'blocking' the word for additional. Times is the multiplication sign, not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Montreux is a town on Lake Geneva in Switzerland, famous for its jazz festival.

clue.text: Composer's offspring embracing her in capital of Ireland

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, an offspring
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of Ireland

explanation.surface: A musician's child hugs his mother in Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is is, linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer of operas and sacred music who worked mainly in Paris.

clue.text: Difficulty with words apparently possesses one acting

parts.note: ap. is a dictionary abbreviation for apparently
has means possesses
the Roman numeral for one
A is an abbreviation for acting, as in a job title

explanation.surface: An actor seems to struggle with lines on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' looks like a hedge on the definition, but it is wordplay, abbreviated to AP as in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphasia is a medical loss of the ability to use or understand language, often after a stroke.

clue.text: Heading away from Thirsk one may ultimately encounter different — person like me?

indicators.note: different signals that the gathered letters are made into a new arrangement
heading away from means the head, the first letter, of Thirsk departs
ultimately points to the last letter of encounter only

explanation.surface: Leaving Thirsk, a traveller may meet someone very unlike the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading away from' leaves HIRSK; with ONE, MAY and R ('ultimately' encounter), 'different' rearranges them. Thirsk is a Yorkshire market town, and Phi, the setter, is a Yorkshireman.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter refers to himself; a Yorkshireman is a man from the English county of Yorkshire, as Phi is.

clue.text: Playing soccer, losing lead, one's subject to pressure

indicators.note: playing signals the letters are put into play and moved around
losing lead tells us the first letter of soccer is dropped

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is a link
on, as in on medication, means subject to

explanation.surface: A footballer playing without a leading role is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing lead' cuts SOCCER to OCCER, which 'Playing' rearranges to COERC.
explanation.definitionFit: Coercion is forcing someone to act by threats or force, a form of pressure.

clue.text: Surrey town: French are almost here

parts.note: es is French for (you) are, from the verb etre

indicators.note: almost tells us here is taken short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A French visitor arriving in a Surrey town is almost here.
explanation.walkthrough: Esher is a commuter town in the English county of Surrey; 'almost' cuts HERE to HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Esher is a town in Surrey, just south-west of London.

clue.text: Unduly vulgar to use station when travelling

indicators.note: travelling things are on the move, so these letters shift into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it crass to use a station while on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link word joining the parts, but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostentatious means showy in a way designed to impress, which reads as excessively vulgar.

clue.text: Risqué photo retained by sexy former lover departing

indicators.note: retained by tells us the photo is kept inside what is left of sexy
departing tells us the former lover leaves the word sexy

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
pic is short for picture, a photo

explanation.surface: An ex walks out but keeps hold of a racy photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departing' takes EX from SEXY to leave SY, and PIC is 'retained by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicy can mean slightly indecent or racy, a close match for risqué.

clue.text: Cough upsets Sir at work

indicators.note: letters at work are being worked over and reshaped into something new

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight is annoyed by a colleague coughing in the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertussis is the medical name for whooping cough, a bacterial infection with violent coughing fits.

clue.text: First person picked up petrol, say, wasting energy? It's a lot to take in

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio means heard, so the word is spelt as it sounds rather than as given

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the letter for energy is dropped

parts.note: petrol is an example of fuel
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A driver muses about filling up with petrol and its wasted energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks petrol as an example of a broader word, and the energy letter is the one wasted from it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is a long look, or a striking sight, so a great deal for the eyes to take in.

clue.text: Improper until each reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters take a new shape

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone behaves badly right up until they are reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unethical conduct breaks moral rules, so it is improper in the sense of wrong.

clue.text: Japanese dish is rejected around European country, with gossip ascribed to Italy

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the little word runs backwards
around means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: is written backwards
the United Kingdom
to yak is to chatter or gossip
I is the international car registration for Italy

explanation.surface: A food story about a Japanese dish turned down by a European diner, with rumours blaming the Italians.
explanation.definitionFit: Sukiyaki is a Japanese hotpot of thinly sliced beef and vegetables simmered at the table.

clue.text: Turning out, say, to involve endless crime and money

indicators.note: to involve tells us the abbreviation for say goes round the other pieces

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

indicators.note: endless tells us the word for crime loses its final letter

parts.note: vice is criminal or immoral activity
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A landlord throws out tenants, say, for being mixed up in crime and money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the example abbreviation, which is made 'to involve' the shortened crime and the money. Tin is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Evicting is expelling tenants from property, which is turning them out.

clue.text: Work in the military force not initially involving too many officers?

indicators.note: in tells us the word for work goes within the shortened military phrase
not initially tells us navy loses its first letter

parts.note: the navy is a military force
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Working in a military service whose ranks are overloaded with officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' strips the first letter from the force, and the work goes 'in' just after the opening letter of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation that is top-heavy has too many senior staff for its base, as with an excess of officers.

clue.text: Supporting college investing in aircraft scheme

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: investing originally means clothing or enclosing, so one piece is wrapped inside another

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A university backs a plan to put money into aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A project is a planned undertaking, a synonym for a scheme or enterprise.

clue.text: India interrupting British finish — good performance, of course

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking in, so the letter sits inside the other piece

parts.note: Br is an abbreviation for British
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to die is to finish or end

explanation.surface: India's cricketers disrupt a British side's finish with a fine display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' is a pun: the good performance happens on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdie is a golf score of one under par on a hole, a good result on the course.

clue.text: Deity put off when given care of Middle East

indicators.note: to be given care of something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: to deter is to put someone off
ME is the abbreviation for Middle East

explanation.surface: A god is reluctant to take charge of the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeter is the Greek goddess of the harvest and agriculture, mother of Persephone.

clue.text: Fan covering latest from top seed

indicators.note: covering the latest part hides the final letter, so it is lost from view

parts.note: a peak is the top
a nut is an enthusiast, a fan

explanation.surface: A supporter backs the tournament's leading seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top seed' reads as a tennis ranking, but seed is the definition and the fan hides the last letter of the word for top.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is the edible seed of a leguminous plant, despite its name not a true nut.

clue.text: Very hard to cut into oral adornment for oral problem

parts.note: too means very or excessively

indicators.note: to cut into is to enter, so the letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: tache is short for moustache, worn round the mouth
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A man finds a moustache too stiff to trim, causing trouble round the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothache is pain in a tooth, a problem located in the mouth.

clue.text: Point about returning materiel?

parts.note: c. stands for circa, about

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: ammo, ammunition, is military supplies

explanation.surface: Someone raises a point about army supplies being sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: Materiel is military equipment and stores; the question mark admits ammunition is only part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma is a punctuation mark, and punctuation marks are commonly called points.

clue.text: 207 in Rome looking bad for the citizens

indicators.note: something looking bad is in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: 207 in Roman numerals, as the next words hint

explanation.surface: A Roman bus route or road number is in a poor state for the people who use it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Rome' tells the solver to write the number as Roman numerals before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic means relating to a city or its citizens, so it fits a phrase about the townspeople.

clue.text: Like oil, filling hole I constructed

indicators.note: filling is the stuffing inside something, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone poured oil into a hole they dug.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleic acid is a fatty acid found in olive oil, and oleic means relating to or derived from oil.

clue.text: Produce something new? Instinctive to retain old version

indicators.note: to retain is to hold on to, so one piece is kept within another

parts.note: innate means inborn or instinctive
O for old and V for version

explanation.surface: Is a natural creator needed to keep the old model going?
explanation.definitionFit: To innovate is to introduce new methods or ideas, bringing forth fresh creations.

clue.text: Kindle vision encompassing return of dead

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word runs backwards
encompassing means surrounding, so the outer word goes round the other

parts.note: sight means vision
late means dead, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A spooky sight of the dead coming back by the light of a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindle also suggests the e-reader, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle a fire is to make it start burning, which is to ignite it.
